Fix ONE confirmed P1 in the reinstated trigger gate. Edit only pipeline/src/agents/pipeline/scenario-trigger-gate.ts and its tests (and the indicator type if needed for typing). DO NOT run git, npm install, or the live pipeline. You MAY run typecheck + targeted vitest.

THE DEFECT (confirmed by adversarial review): scenario-trigger-gate.ts line ~79-81 computes operationalCount with `isOperationalShaped(ind.indicator)` over the WHOLE indicator string. isOperationalShaped uses single-clause parseIndicator (scenario-eval.ts:158), but scenario-eval classifies each indicator PER CLAUSE via parseIndicatorClauses and stamps the result as trigger_kind ('operational' | 'narrative') on each indicator (evaluateIndicator, scenario-eval.ts:272-312 sets out.trigger_kind; the evaluated scenarios' confirming_indicators/invalidating_indicators carry it, scenario-eval.ts:550-552). On a compound indicator like "SPY above 2% while TNX above 4.5%" the two DIVERGE: scenario-eval grades the "SPY above 2%" clause as return-dimension -> trigger_kind='narrative', but isOperationalShaped on the full string lets the yield carve-out (TNX + 2% read as a yield level) return operational=true. Result: a directional all-narrative scenario the lint and trigger_grounding_report count as zero-operational PASSES the gate and reaches decide as tradeable, the exact case the gate exists to block. This is a fail-OPEN and it violates the code's own invariant that the lint count and gate count never drift (scenario-eval.ts:153-156).

THE FIX:
1. operationalCountFix: in applyScenarioTriggerGate, count an indicator as operational when its stamped `trigger_kind === 'operational'`. Read the per-indicator trigger_kind that scenario-eval already computed (the gate always runs AFTER evaluateScenarioTriggers in analyze.ts, so post-eval indicators carry it). Fall back to `isOperationalShaped(ind.indicator ?? '')` ONLY when trigger_kind is absent/undefined (defensive, e.g. the gate invoked on a pre-eval scenario). Keep everything else (the triggerCount>0 && operationalCount===0 rule, directional fail / non-directional downgrade, gated_decide_inputs, note-freeness) exactly as is.
2. typeHandling: the indicator objects in Scenario.confirming_indicators/invalidating_indicators may be typed without trigger_kind (that field lives on IndicatorWithEval in scenario-eval.ts:205, or on the base indicator type). Read trigger_kind in a type-safe way: either widen the indicator type the gate accepts to include an optional trigger_kind?: 'operational' | 'narrative', or read it through the IndicatorWithEval type / a narrow local type. Do NOT use `any`. Keep typecheck clean.
3. testAdded: add a test to pipeline/test/scenario-trigger-gate.test.ts that would have caught this: a DIRECTIONAL scenario whose only trigger is a compound string that isOperationalShaped(full string) would call operational (use the yield carve-out case, e.g. "SPY above 2% while TNX above 4.5%") but whose stamped trigger_kind is 'narrative'. Assert the gate marks it gate_status='fail' and excludes it from gated_decide_inputs (i.e. the gate trusts trigger_kind, not the raw-string reshape). Also add/adjust a case proving that when trigger_kind is absent the fallback still uses isOperationalShaped (so existing single-clause fixtures keep working). Make the fixtures set trigger_kind explicitly to mirror post-eval reality.

Then run `npx tsc --project tsconfig.typecheck.json` (report typecheckExit) and `npx vitest run test/scenario-trigger-gate.test.ts test/decide-scenario-trigger-gate.test.ts` (report gateTestResult pass/fail). diffSummary: the one-line change to the operational count + the type handling + the new test. selfCheck: confirm note-freeness preserved (no support_class/notes), the divergence is closed (gate now agrees with trigger_kind), and the fallback path.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: no attribution, no em dashes in comments, no session links.
